greet.text: Easy - you're no bandit. Brannoc, scout for the Riverwatch garrison. That circle behind me has been glowing since the new moon. The captain wants to know why. I want to know why it hums when I'm not looking at it.

choices.text: Elves raised these stones, didn't they?
Riverwatch sends scouts out alone now?

greet_again.text: Changed your mind about the stones?

lore.text: Older than Riverwatch, older than the road. The stories say the stones keep something asleep. The stories also say a lot of things after the third ale.

lore_elf.text: So your people's songs say. Then maybe you'll understand it better than a garrison scout. Will you take a look?

alone.text: Riverwatch sends scouts out alone when it doesn't have enough scouts. Which is always.

choices.text: I'll look into the stones for you.

accept.text: Good. Touch the crystal if you dare - and look around the circle for anything that broke off it. Folk say shards of the old stones turn up after a storm.

choices.text: The crystal answered when I touched it. Fire ran up my arm.

hint_shards.text: Fire. Of course it was fire. Then it's waking, whatever it is. Find what broke off it - three pieces, if the old tale is right.

decide.text: Three of them. Still warm. The scholars in Riverwatch would pay a fortune to study these... but I've heard the old tales too. Maybe they belong to the stones.

choices.text: They should go back to the stones.

given.text: Sixty gold from the garrison purse, and the captain will hear your name. I hope we're not making a mistake.

chose_stones.text: Then put them back yourself - I'm not touching that crystal. I'll tell the captain the circle is... being tended.

waiting_on_stones.text: Still carrying those shards? The crystal's that way. I'll be here, at a respectful distance.

after_given.text: The scholars are beside themselves. Riverwatch owes you - I'll make sure the captain remembers it.

after_restored.text: The circle's light is steadier now. Calmer. Whatever you did, the humming's stopped keeping me up at night.
